<br />

> [!NOTE]
> **Note:** The Memory Inspector panel is available from Chrome 91. You can check your version at `chrome://version/`.

Use the **Memory inspector** to inspect `ArrayBuffer`, `TypedArray`, and `DataView` memory in JavaScript as well as `WebAssembly.Memory` of Wasm applications written in C++.

## Overview

The **Memory inspector** organizes memory content and helps you navigate large arrays quickly. You can view the ASCII values of memory content directly next to the bytes, and select different endianness. Use the **Memory inspector** while you debug your web app for an efficient workflow.

## Open the Memory Inspector

There are a few ways to open the **Memory inspector**.

### Open from the menu

1. [Open DevTools](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/open).
2. Click **More Options** ![More](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/memory-inspector/image/more-0d3265891c0d3.png) \> **More tools** \> **Memory inspector** . ![Memory inspector menu](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/memory-inspector/image/memory-inspector-menu-59bf7cfcb0055.png)

### Open during debugging

1. Open a page with JavaScript `ArrayBuffer`. We will be using [this demo page](https://chrome.dev/devtools-memory-inspector/).
2. [Open DevTools](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/open).
3. Open the **demo-js.js** file in the **Sources** panel, set a breakpoint at line 18.
4. Refresh the page.
5. Expand the **Scope** section on the right **Debugger** pane.
6. You can open the **Memory inspector**:

   - **From the icon** . Clicking on the icon next to the `buffer` property, or
   - **From the context menu** . Right-click on the `buffer` property and select **Reveal in Memory Inspector panel**.

   ![Reveal in Memory Inspector panel](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/memory-inspector/image/reveal-memory-inspector-c768cdcb79abf.png)

### Inspect multiple objects

1. You can inspect [DataView](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/DataView) or [TypedArray](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/TypedArray) as well. For example, `b2` is a `TypedArray`. To inspect that, right click on the `b2` property and select **Reveal in Memory Inspector panel** (No icon for `TypedArray` or `DataView` yet).
2. A new tab is opened in the **Memory inspector** . Please note that you can inspect multiple objects at once. ![New tab in the Memory inspector](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/memory-inspector/image/new-tab-the-memory-inspe-a4d6eda41779c.png)

## The Memory inspector

![The Memory inspector](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/memory-inspector/image/the-memory-inspector-70f7e3e68c1c9.jpg)

The **Memory inspector** consists of 3 main areas:

### Navigation bar

![Navigation bar](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/memory-inspector/image/navigation-bar-7c8f5070b8dac.jpg)

1. The **address input** shows the current byte address in hex format. You can input a new value to jump to a new location in the memory buffer. For example, try type `0x00000008`.
2. Memory buffers could be longer than a page. Instead of scrolling through, you can use the **left** and **right** button to navigate.
3. The buttons on the left allow a **forward/backward** navigation.
4. By default, the buffer is automatically updated on stepping. In the case it's not, the **refresh** button gives you the option to refresh the memory and update its contents.

### Memory buffer

![Memory buffer](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/memory-inspector/image/memory-buffer-a7d31525c1a55.jpg)

1. From the left, the **address** is displayed in hex format.
2. The **memory** is also shown in hex format, each byte separated by a space. The currently selected byte is highlighted. You can click on the byte or navigate with keyboard (left, right, up, down).
3. An **ASCII representation** of the memory is shown on the right side. A highlight shows the corresponding value to the selected bits on the byte. Similar to memory, you can click on the byte or navigate with keyboard (left, right, up, down).

### Value inspector

![Value inspector](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/memory-inspector/image/value-inspector-5c0c254c78f07.jpg)

1. A top toolbar features a button to switch between **big and little endian** and to open the **settings** . Open the **settings** to select which value types they want to see per default in the inspector. ![toolbar button](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/memory-inspector/image/toolbar-button-54ea370aa3da2.png)
2. The main area shows all the **value interpretations** as per the **settings**. By default, all are shown.
3. The **encoding** is clickable. You can switch between dec, hex, oct for integer and sci, dec for floats. ![Encoding switch](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/memory-inspector/image/encoding-switch-f6cf904c7c193.png)

## Inspecting memory

Let's inspect the memory together.

1. Follow these steps to [start](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/memory-inspector#open-debug) the debugging.
2. Change the address to `0x00000027` in the **address input** . ![address input](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/memory-inspector/image/address-input-418b7229e3036.png)
3. Observe the **ASCII representation** and the **value interpretations**. All values are empty at the moment.
4. Notice the blue **Jump to address** button next to `Pointer 32-bit` and `Pointer 64-bit`. You can click on it to jump to the address. The buttons are grayed out and not clickable if the addresses are not valid. ![Jump to address button](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/memory-inspector/image/jump-address-button-d67529b88b035.png)
5. Click on **Resume script execution** to step through the code. ![Resume script execution](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/memory-inspector/image/resume-script-execution-335bab3a6b807.png)
6. Notice the **ASCII representation** is now updated. All the **value interpretations** are updated as well. ![All value interpretations are updated](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/memory-inspector/image/all-value-interpretations-7031b3861113f.png)
7. Let's customize the **Value inspector** to show only **floating point** . Click on the **settings** button and check only **Float 32-bit** and **Float 64-bit** . ![settings to customize value inspector](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/memory-inspector/image/settings-customize-value-b0cab734b0874.png)
8. Let's change the encoding from `dec` to `sci`. Notice the value representations are updated accordingly. ![Change the encoding.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/memory-inspector/image/change-encoding-6485e8149b9a6.png)
9. Try to navigate the memory buffer with your keyboard or using the navigation bar. Repeat step 4 to observe values changes.

## WebAssembly memory inspection

The `WebAssembly.Memory` object is an `ArrayBuffer` that holds the raw bytes of object memory. The **Memory Inspector** panel lets you inspect such objects in Wasm applications written in C++.

To take full advantage of `WebAssembly.Memory` inspection:

- Use Chrome 107 or later. Check your version at `chrome://version/`.
- Install the [C/C++ DevTools Support (DWARF)](https://chrome.google.com/webstore/detail/cc%20%20-devtools-support-dwa/pdcpmagijalfljmkmjngeonclgbbannb) extension. This is a plugin for debugging C/C++ WebAssembly applications using DWARF debug information.

To inspect the `WebAssembly.Memory` of an object:

1. [Open DevTools](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/open) on [this demo page](https://chrome.dev/devtools-memory-inspector/demo-cpp.html).
2. In the **Sources** panel, open `demo-cpp.cc` and [set a breakpoint](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/javascript/breakpoints#loc) in the `main()` function at line 15: `x[i] = n - i - 1;`.
3. Reload the page to run the application. The debugger pauses at the breakpoint.
4. In the **Debugger** pane, expand **Scope** \> **Local**.
5. Click the ![Reveal in Memory Inspector.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/memory-inspector/image/reveal-memory-inspector-c77ee60001d05.png) icon next to the `x: int[10]` array.

   Alternatively, right-click the array and select **Reveal in Memory Inspector panel**.

![The x array opened in Memory Inspector.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/memory-inspector/image/the-x-array-opened-memor-0d0231bd45de.png)

> [!NOTE]
> **Note:** Starting from Chrome version 107, the **Memory Inspector** highlights all the bytes of a C/C++ memory object. This lets you tell them apart from the surrounding memory.

To stop highlighting object memory, in the **Memory Inspector** panel, hover over the object badge and click the `x` button.

![Stop highlighting object memory.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/memory-inspector/image/stop-highlighting-object-3b446e810ccbd.png)

To learn more, see:

- [Extending the Memory Inspector for C/C++ debugging](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/memory-inspector-extended-cpp)
- [Debugging WebAssembly with modern tools](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/wasm-debugging-2020).
